subject: Demo request: Dedicated capacity & autoscale behavior — Corelytics

From: Anna Morales <anna@corelytics.ai>

Cc: 
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Demo request: Dedicated capacity for real-time inference

Hi Hannah,

We signed up through the self-serve flow yesterday and wanted to follow up to schedule a quick live walkthrough focused on Dedicated capacity and autoscaling behavior. We’re evaluating Redwood for a production feature that will serve low-latency, high-throughput responses from a quantized LLM. A few details:

- Production traffic profile: bursts to ~200 QPS for short periods, sustained ~40 QPS.
- Target p95 latency: <= 60ms for generation fragments (token streaming acceptable).
- Typical sequence lengths: 64–1024 tokens (95% under 256).
- Must understand cold-start behavior, autoscaling, and prefix/KV cache effects.

Attached is a one-page requirements doc with sample queries and expected SLA language. Could you share availability for a 45–60 minute demo with an engineering-focused section? We’re PST-based (San Francisco).

Thanks,
Anna Morales
Senior Product Manager
Corelytics
Attachment: Corelytics_demo_requirements.pdf

Hi all — Ben here (Solutions Engineering). Quick technical notes so the demo is actionable:

1) Throughput and latency: 200 QPS bursts are achievable with Dedicated if we size the pool and pick the right model/quantization. We’ll want to confirm: average tokens per request, max concurrent requests per client, and whether streaming partial tokens is acceptable for latency targets.

2) Cold starts & autoscale: Redwood Dedicated supports fast warmup when KV caching is used and when route pinning is configured. For unpredictable bursts we recommend a small baseline pool + aggressive burst capacity with a warm standby. We’ll demo both a canary and fallback plan.

3) Model artifacts: bring your model architecture (or tell us which open model you plan to use). If you plan to push a quantized 4-bit variant, we’ll talk kernel selection and memory planning.

Slots: I’m UK-based tomorrow and those early PDT slots conflict with a customer ramp. Could we shift the 2:00pm PDT slot to 3:30pm PDT (that’s 11:30pm my time, I can make it) or do 9:00am PDT on Fri work for Corelytics?

I’ll prepare a short load script and a demo plan that shows both steady-state throughput and a simulated burst to demonstrate autoscale and tail latency.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
